utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good afternoon, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. All the accused are here. Mr. Mrkic from the Beara team is absent. Rest, I think, are here. Prosecution are Mr. McCloskey accompanied by Mr. Thayer. All right. Witness is in the -- is present. Good afternoon to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to proceed with your cross-examination. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a couple of questions, and thereby conclude my cross-examination. As you remember yesterday, we stopped when -- while we were discussing the search of the terrain. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the case where you testified previously and, if need be, we are going to give references, inter alia, you mentioned that this search was commanded by Mr. Gavric from the Bratunac Brigade. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is your recollection such that you would answer in the same manner to this question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion you said that the order to search the terrain, as you repeated yesterday, you received in the command of the Bratunac Brigade on the 17th of July, between 7.00 and 8.00, but in yesterday's transcript it was stated between 8.00 and 9.00. My question is, where did you receive this order, and to the best of your memory, when this was done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, that meeting took place in the command of the Bratunac Brigade. Whether there were any other evidence, records, as to the order, I'm trying to remember. It could -- it is possible that some order was recorded from the commander of the special police brigade. I'm trying to recall that to testify about that here. In my talks with the Prosecutor I saw that order, I did not remember it previously. I would like to take a look at it once again so that I could give you an exact answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now, I would like to ask the usher to retrieve Exhibit 4D97, and before we have it on the screen may I explain that it goes for a map of the area that you were located in, and with the help of the usher we would ask you to mark your position on the 17th and the 18th of July, by this I mean the area which you combed or searched on these dates. If we may enlarge this area along this road. Excellent, thank you. Sir, let's take a look at this map together. The red line marks the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the right-hand side is Bratunac, to the left, Konjevic Polje. Do you agree about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the village of Kravica being marked here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Further down the road can you see Lolici, the village of Lolici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We'll be able to spot in large letters to the left-hand side of the road in the direction of Konjevic Polje the area of the village Pobudje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like Madam Usher to help you mark the area where you moved on the 17th and 18th of July, 1995, while searching this area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, do you think it will be beneficial if we zoomed in the area of Kravica that you were referring the witness to, at least to an extent? I mean it would help everyone read the names first -- in the first place. We know where they were, but some people don't. And if we zoom in then he can mark on the zoomed-in copy. I think it will be more useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see a problem with that, Your Honour, although marking out the territory would entail the need to have a broader view of the area. But I would like to ask for the witness to focus on the toponyms of Siljkovici and Kravica, along this red line marking the road. This would be the third quadrant from the right-hand side of the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, may I ask you to circle with the stylus you are going to be given, the area marked out as Kravica on that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please also mark out the village of Lolici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let us zoom out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can't zoom in and out, et cetera. He started marking this map. Where would you wish him to mark out now?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Then I would like you, Witness, to mark out the first circle with the letter K.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And a circle denoting the village of Lolici, to mark it by the letter L?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And in the top right corner, could you please write PW-160.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And in the bottom right corner, could you please state the date, the 13th of March, 2007?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, while we're still working on this map, could you mark in the bottom right corner the direction of Bratunac by the letter B, and in the opposite direction KP, denoting Konjevic Polje, and further markings are going to be made on another map. If I could ask for the initial view. Thank you. Could we zoom in to the area of the village of Pobudje? Excellent, thank you. Sir, I will ask you to mark the right-hand side of the road with BR, standing for Bratunac, and in the opposite direction on the left-hand side, to state KP, to denote Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Now, could you please mark out the area in which you searched terrain on the 17th and 18th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] Roughly here, in this area. I don't know exactly the line of departure, I cannot remember, but mainly I know that Bratunac Brigade was up to, along the road, then there were we and then to the left of us were the military brigade, which was connected with us on our left flank.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark out the direction of your movement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark with an arrow the direction of movement of the members of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that with an BRB. BRB for Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark out the direction of movement of the military [as interpreted] brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may say this, I was -- it was pointed out to me that on page 6 in line 5 and in 7, in 18 -- in 5 and 18th [as interpreted] it states "military" instead of Milici Brigade. May this be rectified so that we know exactly which unit we're discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. We are through with this document. But before that could we mark it. Sir, could you please mark it -- this view with PW-160, and above that could you date this map, 13th of March, 2007?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we conclude work on this document, and now I would like to ask for us to take a look in the e-court, Exhibit 4D83. And 4D83. Before we have it on the screen, I would like to explain that this is the order of the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, dated 14th of July, 1995. I believe that this document has been translated into English. If I could ask for it to be juxtaposed to the B/C/S version, focusing on item -- item 1 of the document issued by the commander of the Bratunac Brigade to the effect that on the basis of an order from the command of the Drina Corps, and with a view of executing a complete search of the liberated territory, the same should be done in accordance with a detailed instruction in -- under items 1, 2, 3, and 4 of this order. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that under 1, item 1, the area between Lupoglav and Ravni Buljib, and then along the axes around the village of Sandic, that that denotes the area that you departed from in your search of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the details, but we searched part of this terrain depending on the number of men that we had at our disposal and that we were given.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Under item 6 of this order it reads that "personnel involved in the search will wear white bands on their right shoulders for purposes of recognition and identification." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that you and your troops wore those white bands which served the purpose of identification?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let us take a look at Exhibit 4D86.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it has also been translated into English. And before we have it on the screen, I would like to explain that this document is a proposal by Colonel Ignjat Milanovic from the Drina Corps to the commander of the Drina Corps dated 15th of July, 1995. I would like -- ask to focus on a section that is on page 2 of the English version. Item 1 of the proposal. In the B/C/S we are on the right page. In the English version we will have to go back to page 1, to the last row or paragraph. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, take a look at this proposal, which says that after the state of affairs had been stated the proposal is to authorise and appoint the commander of the 1st Bratunac Brigade as commander of all forces which are participating in the search of the terrain and for the sweeping of the battlefield to the east of the road and in control of the Kasaba-Drinjaca road. My question to you is, is it known to you that the commander of the Bratunac Brigade was appointed as commander of all forces taking part in the search of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that, but I do know what kind of reports we sent from the field, and I know that information was sent through Captain Gavric to the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From your yesterday's testimony I understood that from Mr. Borovcanin you received an instruction to contact Momir Nikolic a day earlier for further instructions and further orders. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes, that was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, I would like to take a look at Prosecution Exhibit P00262, which has also been translated into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And before we see it on the screen, Your Honours, I would like to explain that this was a regular combat report of the commander of the 1st Bratunac Brigade dated 18th July 1995, submitted to the commander of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask to focus on item 2 of this combat report, which states -- if you can follow what I'm saying, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: "Our units -- during the day our units and the 3rd Infantry Battalion and 4th Infantry Battalion and people mobilised for compulsory labour have searched the terrain in the area of Pubudje, Glogova, Hrncici, and Konjevic Polje." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the area where you moved on that day on the 18th and the day before on the 17th of July, and is that the area that you marked out on the map a couple of minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it known to you that these days, the 16th, the 17th, and the 18th of July, Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin, with the 2nd Sekovici detachment was located in the village of Baljkovica in the Zvornik municipality in combat with the 28th Brigade, which was breaking out of the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were some fighting there that Mr. Borovcanin was in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how far away is that area from the area that you were located in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly from Bratunac to Zvornik there is some 40 to 50 kilometres. But I don't know the exact distance to that village that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But we can agree that that distance is over 40 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to conclude my cross-examination with working on Exhibit 4D80.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And before we have it on the screen, Your Honour, may I explain that this is an order of the commander of the Drina Corps dated 13th of July, 1995. Let us take a look at the last paragraph in the B/C/S version of that order, and in the English version. That would be item 4. I believe that's -- that is on the following -- no, no, no, it's not on the following page. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let us focus on this part of the Drina Corps command order. It reads, "Captured and disarmed Muslims are to be accommodated in appropriate premises which can be secured with lower-strength forces, and report on that to the Supreme Command." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's an order about -- issued by the Drina Corps on the 13th of July, 1995. My question to you is, have you personally ever, in that period, on the 12th, 13th and 14th, received any order relating to the treatment of POWs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have received no such order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On those days you never received an order from Ljubomir Borovcanin that your deserters' unit, as we call it, I apologise, should isolate able-bodied Muslim men from their families in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Likewise you never received an order from Ljubomir Borovcanin that your unit of "deserters," in inverted commas, should attack, disarm, or take prisoner any UN soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You never received any instructions regarding the right of your unit of so-called deserters to seize or destroy personal property of Muslims, including their valuables?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If there should have -- if there should have been such events in the field, you personally know nothing about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally know nothing about it, but I saw some objects and some property. I saw some people moving about, but I know nothing personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to -- an additional explanation. You said that you saw property abandoned by the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, before we proceed any further on this, because I think this needs clarification. To your previous question the witness said, "I personally know nothing about it, but I saw objects and some property. I saw some people moving about, but I know nothing personally." Can he explain it better, what he means by he saw some objects and some property, what were -- what was this -- what were these objects, this property, and what he means by saying "people moving about," and also who were these people, whether they were members his group, whether they members of some military unit, or whether they were civilians. Perhaps he can explain. I think it needs clarification, because as it is it is very vague.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, have you understood the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So the question was, you said that you had seen things, objects, abandoned by the roadside. Can you tell us where, in which area, you saw that, whose personal effects or property that -- those were, and what soldiers, if they were soldiers, you saw moving along the road, and what do you mean by these personal effects that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I meant that some bags were being carried, and parcels. And I meant the movement of civilians around Potocari. I don't know anything about military movements. And there were the unit, the deserters' unit, the military police, and other units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I had interrupted you, Mr. Stojanovic, when you had -- you were asking the witness about seeing property abandoned by the road. So you can proceed on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. But I have been warned that on page 12, line 9, the answer was not recorded in full. The witness said that he had seen personal effects, and that he knew nothing about personal ID, and this is not reflected in the transcript. So if you agree, I will repeat the question, and clarify to the full.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You heard what Mr. Stojanovic has just said. Do you agree with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you could repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then repeat, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So, the question was, when you saw that you had seen personal effects by the roadside, did you see abandoned ID documents, such as passports or identification -- identity cards, or do you mean by personal effects bags and the like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see no identification documents, nor passports or identity cards. And as for bags and parcels and et cetera, I saw some.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that we've clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to go into private session for the last two questions because it refers to a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While I'm formatting the question, I would like us to take a look at Exhibit 4D16, this is a Defence Exhibit, and this is a statement about the facts concerning Momir Nikolic, but I apologise, perhaps it would be better if we were to go back to private session, because we will quote some parts of the documents, including names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's do that. Let's go back to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure how expert I am to explain the humanitarian situation in Bijeljina or in Bosanski Novi or any town in Bosnia-Herzegovina, or in the town that I lived in. What I can say is that at that time any -- in any town if you had 10 Deutschmarks, you were a rich man. And with 10 German marks you can -- you could live for months and whoever could afford to buy clothes, trousers, shoes, et cetera, they were considered rich. Many had fled from their homes, both Muslims, Serbs, Croats, lived in other people's homes. Literally I believe that they lived supported by some form of humanitarian aid. This is how I see that situation, not only in a particular town or city, but throughout the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the town we mentioned earlier on, did you have enough water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was water. I think there was enough water because there are two rivers flowing close to that town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that regardless of where this town is, there were water cuts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but there are some shortages or disruptions to the water-supply in the town where I live now for a couple of hours at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether there was enough to eat or enough food in the shops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could buy some food items. Enough, well, that's not for me to say. (redacted) If I were to say there was enough or there wasn't enough, well, I would be mistaken because there was some food to be bought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I know why you are standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam, go ahead and please remember not to mention the town. Or anything else that could identify you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that there was practically no humanitarian aid coming into the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know, believe me. I cannot tell you exactly whether there was some humanitarian aid coming or not. I was never involved in these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about your tasks in Potocari, and you said that your task was, among other things, to ensure security for the UNPROFOR and for the civilians who were gathered there. Is it fair to say that the Serb authorities were afraid that the Serb civilians who might have lost some family during the war may come to Potocari to attack the Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the Serb authorities were afraid that Serb civilians who lived around Potocari, around Srebrenica and Bratunac, and who may have lost some family, some relatives, would come in July 1995 to Potocari to attack Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible, that's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And indeed your task was to protect the Muslim civilians who were in the Potocari base, to protect them from any mistreatment, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task was to secure UNPROFOR forces and to secure the civilians, and for the civilians to be evacuated, for us to assist in their evacuation, so that they may depart in the arranged direction or in the direction which they wanted to take. Because some things had been pre-arranged.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But you say that your task was to ensure the security of the UNPROFOR and of the civilians. Is that not a protection task, as such, so that nothing could happen to them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think he's answered the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so too. Let's move, Ms. Fauveau, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were in Potocari, you went together with General Mladic when he spoke to the Muslim civilians, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And on that occasion water and food was distributed -- were distributed to Muslim civilians, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, food and water were distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that water tanks were brought to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I saw one water tanker. I don't know about the rest, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And that water tank was brought to Potocari for water to be distributed to Muslim civilians. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was General Mladic filmed when he was speaking to the civilians while food was being distributed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And when the crew filming General Mladic left, is it fair to say that nobody ill-treated the Muslim civilians; they were able to eat the food that had been distributed to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, nobody took that food away. I did not see such occurrences.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move to private session for a few questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, will the's move to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you understood the question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood the question. The question is whether, after the war, I learnt about the number of the people there. I don't want this figure that I uttered to be taken as something exact. Maybe there were more people or less people. In my mind it was a huge crowd of people. It was a huge crowd of people, in my opinion. I may be mistaken about the numbers or the figures, but I did not hear after the war what was the exact number. I had no need to listen subsequently to any of that, because I know what I saw. Please do not take my word for granted as to the figures. Because at that moment it did not matter; what figures I do give, they are rough figures.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I agree. So we can conclude that figure you gave is just an approximate figure and that you would agree that it may not be the right figure. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately. When one sees such a crowd one can be mistaken in their assessment of the figure. So I can be mistaken, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned the arrival of buses and you spoke about the behaviour of the Muslim civilians. Is that true that they were not pushed towards their buses, they were in a hurry themselves to get on the buses? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all of them were in a hurry to leave, that's one thing. The second thing, it is possible that some people were pushed. And from the point where they departed from when they set out towards the buses and the trucks, they were running to occupy a place on these vehicles, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you spoke about the part played by the UNPROFOR in the evacuation. Is it fair to say that no UNPROFOR member spoke to you saying that you had -- one had to stop the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. They were there, they must have helped, assisted; they took part in all that. I do not remember that conversation, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that you entered on the 12th July 1995 with a DutchBat officer into the UNPROFOR base of DutchBat. Is it fair to say that this happened before the bus -- the buses arrived, the buses that were meant to evacuate the people from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe -- I think it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were together with that DutchBat officer, did you discuss the evacuation with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that we discussed any evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that you saw men get on the buses separately from the other Muslim civilians. And you added on page 1665, you said that you didn't see when exactly these men were -- where they were separated. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th and on the 13th of July, 1995, is it fair to say that some of the Muslim forces were still around Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that on the 12th, when we were entering Potocari, fire was opened from the left-hand side of the road, and I had information that beyond Potocari the army was going through the woods towards Tuzla. They were taking a route unknown to me, but through the forest and over those hills beyond Potocari. That would be to the right-hand side of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could it be that the men you saw being separated were actually Muslim military men who had been captured and then taken to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you clarify that question for me, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could it be that the men you saw who were being separated from the other civilians had been taken to Potocari after being captured around Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as that question is framed, it's so general that without, I think, further clarification in terms of any basis for his knowledge, it's an improper question as framed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you plan to adduce evidence that this was so, Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you put such a question to the witness, you must be sure that you have a basis for it. You can't put a witness -- a question to the witness based on something hypothetical which you cannot prove.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with all respect, I do not think it is a hypothetical question. I believe we have, indeed, adduced evidence to the effect, but if you prohibit the question, I will not put it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, did you see anyone, any men being separated in the first place? Let's start from there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I saw a column heading towards the buses. A column of men. I did not see any separation of same, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: These men that you saw were, to your knowledge, Muslims or any other kind of ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only say that I presume that they must have been Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Were they accompanied by any Serbian military units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were on their own in a column heading towards the buses and the trucks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't know if it is still the case of you wanting to put the same question again after having heard the witness, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. I could ask him whether he knew where the men came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a fair question. If you could answer it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know where they had come from.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that between the 12th and the 14th of July, 1995, you had an opportunity to go through Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And, when you went through Bratunac, you never saw many bodies of killed people in Bratunac, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bratunac I didn't see one dead body.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that in Potocari, you didn't see bodies of killed people in Potocari either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw no dead bodies in Potocari either.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 9th of March, 2007, page 69 of the transcript, you said that you did not have any contact with Momir Nikolic whilst the Muslim civilians were being evacuated from Potocari. Is it true that you knew him before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I didn't remember any contact with Mr. Nikolic, but I think that I had known him before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you said that you're not sure today whether you knew him before?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: He just answered the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He said he thinks that he knew him before. If you are going to ask him further questions that could reveal his identity, obviously we need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think it would be useful, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you stated that the UNPROFOR members had to escort the convoys to Kladanj, but you didn't know whether the UNPROFOR members had done it, had escorted the convoys. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they really escorted the convoys, the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In 2003 you gave a statement, which I'm not going to mention; we've just spoken about it a moment ago. Do you remember stating that indeed the convoys had been escorted by the UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably that's what I stated. According to the information I had, they should have escorted the convoy. Whether they started escorting it and then stopped or not, I don't know. I heard that they should have escorted it. Whether they escorted it with the UNHCR, I cannot say because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the statement which is still on display. I would like it not to be broadcast. Could we see page 4 in the B/C/S version -- sorry, in English, and page 6 in the B/C/S version. Sir, it's right at the beginning, page 6 in B/C/S. You stated, "[In English] I have to underline that there were UNPROFOR representatives in the vehicles at the head and at the back of the convoy, heading towards Kladanj." [Interpretation] Can you confirm that the UNPROFOR vehicles were at the front and at the back of the convoys going to Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, and I have said so already, they were leading the convoy. I don't know whether there were any at the back. Whether they stopped driving along at the back, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Fauveau. Who wishes to go next? We should have the break in three minutes' time. So I think we can have it now. Who is going next after the break? Ms. Nikolic, all right. We will have a 25-minute break starting from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Nikolic. Ms. Nikolic is appearing for Accused Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only have one question to ask you. Listening carefully to your testimony in the past few days, you testified to many events in which you personally took part in the summer of 1995. You testified to the situation in Potocari, Bratunac, you explained the order of the minister of the interior of the Republika Srpska from July 1995. What I would like to ask you, when you sum up all these events, do you agree with me that the decisions regarding everything that ensued, including the events in which you took part, were the results or the consequences of a decision taken at a high political level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on that, but I can say that most probably, yes, it is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Nikolic. Who is next? Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will not cross-examine this witness, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Ostojic, or Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. The Gvero Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Likewise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Haynes for Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: We don't have questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there re-examination? Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I do, and I will be as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Other than hearing about the incident at the Kravica hangar, did you receive any information about any prisoners surrendering to or being captured by Jahorina or special police brigade units along that road on the 12th or the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received information that along the road and around the road something was happening, that there was a complicated situation. I would like to know what was going on in that area at the time too.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So just to clarify, based on that answer, is your answer that you did not receive any information about prisoners surrendering or being captured along that road other than what you testified about concerning the prisoners at the Kravica hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received information that some were surrendering and some were being taken prisoner, but I didn't know what -- what would happen -- what happened afterward. Whether they were taken somewhere or whatever happened to them. I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is it your understanding that that information that you just referred to that you received concerned those prisoners who ended up at the Kravica hangar? Just to clarify.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I can't say, because I simply don't know where they ended up. About the Kravica hangar, I have already said what I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, do you recall anything in particular at all about who gave you this information or when, about prisoners surrendering or being captured?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, this is the third time, three questions in a row asking for the same information and he's coming back again for more clarification. Whenever the Defence is doing cross-examination, my colleague gets up at first question saying, "question asked and answered." We waited three times, I think maybe he should move on to another line of questioning. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The last question, I may have agreed with you in relation to the first and second, but this is seeking information as to who gave him information. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly, Your Honours. I think that this question has already been answered twice, only it was differently phrased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer. Do you wish to respond? I think there is a very clear answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm simply trying to identify, when he is referring to information, what information he's talking about and when he received it. I think the record, frankly, is just a little unclear on that point, whether he received any information other than information about the individuals at Kravica, and, if he did, when did he receive that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That changes it a little bit. I tried -- I tried to explain why at least your last question was in order. And that was precisely because you were seeking from the witness information as to who had given him information; now you change it. Now you change it. So as long as you stick to your last question, that is your last question as it was before. Yeah. So let's start with that. I mean, I don't think we should lose much time on this, actually. It's very clear. First he answered that he received information that some were surrendering, some were being -- and he doesn't know anything else. Then he confirmed that he didn't know where they ended up. Then you asked him who gave him the information that he relayed to us. And you were stopped. Now you're saying when you received this information and which particular information, I think, which particular information we already know. So please restrict your question to who gave him the information and when he received that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we'll move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand His Honour's clarification and intervention there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you think you can answer the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You've referred earlier on to receiving some information that some of the Muslims were surrendering and some were being taken prisoners, but you don't know what happened afterwards. Now, who gave you this information? And when did you get this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't remember when I received that information. If I mention a date I will say a lie. But I know that that information reached me, but from what level, believe me, I don't remember. Believe me, I really don't remember. I got such information, and that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Let me ask just one follow-up question and I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You testified about learning about this incident at the Kravica warehouse soon after you believe it occurred. Other than that occasion when you received information about something happening at the Kravica warehouse, did you receive any other reports about any prisoners being taken along the road on the 12th or 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but this is a repetition. Move -- thank you, Mr. Bourgon. I mean, I spared you a few words.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead. Your previous question was very clear because it was apart from what happened at Kravica, in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, page 9 at line 18 of today's transcript you were asked a question about Mr. Borovcanin's being in the vicinity of Balkovici in the Zvornik municipality from July 16th to July 18th. I want to ask you, under the law, as my learned friend Mr. Stojanovic reviewed with you yesterday, what was your understanding if MUP units were operating in Balkovici in Zvornik municipality at that time, to which brigade would those MUP units have been resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked a series of questions by I believe a couple of my learned colleagues about your contacts with Momir Nikolic in Potocari. I want to ask you if it would help your recollection to learn about the testimony of a Dutch officer that this Trial Chamber has already heard. If I read that back to you, would that refresh your recollection or help your recollection at all about any contacts you may have had with Mr. Momir Nikolic on that day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, these are questions already asked by the Prosecutor in their examination-in-chief. I do not think that this comes from the cross-examination at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It comes from the examination because -- from the cross-examination because you asked the witness and even confronted him with previous statements of Momir Nikolic, as to whether he met Momir Nikolic on the particular occasion that we spoke about. So Witness said that he, as far as he could remember, he didn't. But he -- Mr. Thayer is now seeking to refresh his memory, but it's perfectly in order. Let me consult with my colleagues in case they think I am wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. As you may have noticed, we've had a lengthy discussion. Also weighing the different positions at law, and in particular what also happened in examination, during the examination-in-chief. I think we have come to -- not I think, we have come to the conclusion that the question is perfectly in order. The reason is that it arises mainly as a result of the witness being -- having his memory tested again, and by Madam Fauveau, during her cross-examination, which should open the way to a further question related to that. Yes, so go ahead, but if the witness doesn't remember, then we close that chapter and we'll move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Absolutely, Mr. President. And if we may move into private session for this one question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall being asked this afternoon about any water tanks being brought into Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I believe your recollection was that there was one. I want to show you a video clip that begins at 2 hours, 27 minutes and 40 seconds and runs to 2 hours, 28 minutes flat. So it's an approximately 20-second video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just want to ask you, sir, is that the water tank to which you were referring in your answer, or was there another water tank that you were recalling?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that it would be only fair to specify the time relevant for this question, because this video footage dates from the 13th of July. And this should be given to the witness before he is supposed to answer, because the witness stated that he wasn't there on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's a very fair remark.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just -- and I perfectly agree, Your Honour. With the exception of the characterisation of his testimony about whether or not he was on the 13th. That is a fair question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course it is. Of course it is. On the other hand, he also mentioned that he only saw one tank to his knowledge, so it is also perfectly legitimate to ask him whether this could be the one that he saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you understand the back and forth among His Honour and my learned friend and myself, Witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can circumvent it in a very easy way, whether he remembers the tank that he saw on the particular day when he saw it to have the UN markings on it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So he can't answer the other question that you may have wished to put to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to show you one more video clip, sir, which you were -- well, we'll just show you the video clip and then we will proceed. This is at 2 hours, 22 minutes, to 2 hours, 22 minutes, 40 seconds, again another short clip. You were asked some questions, sir, concerning separation of men. I believe you testified that you recall seeing a column of men. And I want to show you a video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you -- do you recall being shown that video clip by the investigator in 2000, during your interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall being shown that in my office last week sometime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, aside from those two occasions when you were shown this video segment, is it your testimony that you have any other independent recollection of seeing any groups of separated men on the 12th or 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already stated that I saw a separated group of men on the 12th or the 13th, and that there was General Mladic there and somebody else, and this is what I said. I've testified to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Just to clarify, when you refer to General Mladic and a group of men, you're referring to your testimony concerning some men that were gathered at a flat area alongside the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac communication; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So, referring to what is depicted in this video clip, sir, is your testimony that you recall seeing a group of Muslim men actually in a column passing buses, or is it your testimony that you simply have seen this video clip on two prior occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be frank, I can't remember in this respect. I see here that men were separated, and as far as I know, at that time I did see the movement of these men. And I saw them board the buses, but whether they were separated or not, where they were headed, that I don't know, and I know that I took no part in all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Thayer. Sir, we've come to the end of your testimony because we don't have any further questions for you. Our staff will assist you to facilitate your return back home at the earliest. On behalf of the Tribunal, I wish you -- I thank you for having come over to give testimony, and I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe all the parties have the tender sheet. A couple of them may require just some explanation. The -- Your Honours may recall I actually showed a colour -- an original piece of evidence thinking that would best help refresh his recollection. Because it was original evidence, I had to have him mark a black and white copy of that. What I have to tender to the Court is a colour copy of the original piece of evidence unmarked to assist the Court in seeing what was actually shown to him, to refresh his recollection. Plus we have the marked black and white version that he marked with a black magic marker during his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. First, I take it that, as Mr. Thayer stated, you all have received a copy of the documents to be tendered through this Prosecution witness. Are there any objections to any of them? We hear none. So they are all admitted. I don't see any -- yeah. They are so all -- all admitted. And the one under number 5 remains under seal. No, sorry. Okay. Are there any of them -- yes, it's P02473 that remains under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's take the -- and these clips that you have made use of in your redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, those are all part of P02047, which is already admitted. If it helps to save some time, I can represent to the Court that we have no objections to the Borovcanin team's documents that are on their tender sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Are there any objections from any of the other Defence teams to the documents that the Borovcanin Defence team seeks to tender? Okay. We hear none. So they are all admitted. Those marked to be kept under seal will remain under seal. I just want to make sure. Okay. On the face of it, I done see any others that should be kept under seal, but please check. Madam Fauveau, do you wish to tender any documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that there are no other documents to be tendered. So we can move to the next witness. I see Mr. Elderkin here, waiting. Yes, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I return briefly to the matter that I think was raised in private session by my learned friend Mr. Bourgon, the objection to the re-examination. The Chamber understandably said it made no determination in relation to those various submissions. If the matter is going to be considered in due course, can we be permitted to make some submissions in relation to this particular issue? The position is that so far as that witness was concerned, we had no real interest, frankly, or standing therefor. But generally, we do take a stance in relation to this. And the matter we would suggest, could be aired at a convenient moment sometime in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the it was your Prosecution's understanding, frankly that that general issue had been decided by the Chamber previously. If the Court desires, we can make submissions as well. I don't think we were doing anything that was out of the practise of the Trial Chamber thus far, so I'm not sure if -- if there is a -- a need for further filings on this issue. But we remain at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As you may have noticed, we took some time to discuss, and there is further ground for -- ground for further discussions. So we'll come back to you whether we require further submissions on it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Any guidance would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the time being, let's not take more of our court time and proceed with the next witness. And before he comes in, and before we proceed, you will recall that we discussed him briefly when we were dealing with the Prosecution motion to convert 12 witnesses to 92 ter witnesses, and I had a confirmation then from both sides, from all sides, actually, that as regards the next witness there was no controversy, no disagreement, there was no objection to have him converted into a 92 ter witness, but going through the transcripts of the 1st and 8th of March, I noticed, or rather we noticed, because we've been discussing this, that we never decided that motion in relation to the next witness, Peccerelli. So we are deciding that motion now, acceding -- granting the motion. The rest of the motion, as it regards the 11 other witnesses remains -- remains with the Trial Chamber, and we will come back to you when we are in a position to decide it. Mr. Elderkin, I suppose you would be taking -- leading this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. There was an issue that I wished to raise before the next witness to ensure that we could maybe have some guidance from the Trial Chamber before the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you want to make the submission in his absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It doesn't matter because it's something technical about the Trial Chamber's decision dated the 6th March, and that is the decision regarding the Prosecution's Rule 94 bis notice, a decision that was rendered by the Trial Chamber on the 6th of March. It is our -- today, it being the 13th of March, this is our dead-line to raise certification or to request certification of this decision. And we have been actively considering the matter amongst the Defence teams. There are things that we are not clear about the decision, and as it stands now we would prefer, instead of asking for certification, to ask the Trial Chamber for some clarification and guidance concerning this decision, and we would like to have a further delay of two days before we can file this in writing to ask clarification concerning this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I personally have no problems. No problem. We have no -- no problems on our part.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. This was a request made on behalf of all teams.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, it's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And we will file this request two days from now and then we don't know yet if it's going to be at that time a joint motion or a partly joined motion. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Bourgon. Let's bring the witness in. Yes, Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, while we're waiting for the witness to come in, I just would clarify the procedure I will follow with the witness. Given his status, both as an expert and under 92 ter, I will merely ask about five or 10 minutes' of questions in direct. I'm not going to actually read out a summary of his written report, which is already in evidence as an expert statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You've got the Chamber's authorisation to do that, or to proceed that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal, with which you're familiar. Before you start your testimony, could I kindly ask you to make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shall I raise my hand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, you don't need to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Please take a seat, make yourself comfortable. You're familiar with the procedure. You are a 92 ter witness, and perhaps that has already been explained to you. Mr. Elderkin will put some questions to you. If you have ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: May I start by asking you to say your name, please?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: My name is Fredy Peccerelli.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: I'm a forensic anthropologist. I'm the executive director of the Guatemalan Forensic Anthropology Foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can you give us a brief summary of your qualifications, bearing in mind that we have already seen a copy of your CV.

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: For the last 12 years, I have worked in the exhumation, recovery, and analysis of human remains, mostly from the mass graves that are a result of Guatemalan human-armed conflict, and as a result from that I have gained experience in locating graves, also in analysis of the remains. My educational background is a bachelor's degree in anthropology and a master's course in forensic and biological anthropology.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us where you studied?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: City University of New York, Brooklyn college, and Bournemouth University in the United Kingdom.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us about the first time you worked in Bosnia, when was that?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: That was in 1997, in a site called Brcko, which was close to the border with Croatia. It was, I believe, the first ICTY team, and together, myself from Guatemala and a couple others from Peru, the United Kingdom, and the United States as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And again, after that, I understand that you worked in Bosnia on a number of other occasions?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Yes, I was called back to also contribute with the recovery of human remains in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1998. Zeleni Jadar, for example, was one of the sites I worked that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Turning now to the work that you did on Srebrenica-related graves in 2000, could you tell us about the role you had?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: During the 2000 season I was named deputy senior director of the recovery team, or the archaeology team. In the absence of Professor Richard Wright, I was to head the team and work specifically in the site called Lazete 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: We've seen your Lazete 1 report, but perhaps you could tell us briefly what your findings were concerning that grave site?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: In that specific site we found a grave of about 15 metres in length by about five metres in width, of a depth of about a metre 50, that contained about 127 bodies, human bodies. We also found two bodies in a ditch nearby. One of the things that I remember clearly from the site is that about 89 of the bodies had pieces of material around their heads, some of them covering their eyes directly - we called those probable blindfolds - and overall from that site we recover, I think, 735 items of evidence, 129 of those were bodies, and the rest were artefacts and some body parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And were you involved in the autopsy work on those human remains at the mortuary?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: No, not at that time. At that time my task was specifically to find the grave, recover its contents, make sure that the chain of custody was intact, and then place the bodies in a -- in a container, in a refrigerated container, and send the bodies down to the morgue in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: If I can just ask you about the nature of the grave itself rather than the remains therein. Could you tell if that grave had been disturbed prior to your excavation?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Well, that grave was -- initially we could tell -- well, we started by scraping the surface, and eventually, as in most graves that weigh found in Bosnia, a blue-ish yellow -- a blue-ish greenish colour clay allowed us to find this grave. We found the outline and we could see it was irregular in some points, but we found a concentration of bodies, three. Two of them were separated and in those two areas of bodies that were separated you could tell that there was only body parts of the soil fill was a bit different, and it was clear to us at that time that the bodies that were there had been removed. So there was two events, the event of the initial excavation of the grave, and then a -- another event where some of the bodies were removed from the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can I ask you now, did you work on any other Srebrenica-related graves in the summer?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Yes, while I was there I was asked to also take a look at the site that was just on the other side of the railway in Lazete as well; that would be Lazete 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And when you were asked to work on that site, did you know that was the first time that Lazete 2 had been excavated?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: I was told in 1996 an ICTY PHR, Physicians for Human Rights, recovery team had exhumed some bodies from the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can you, the same as you did with your brief summary of Lazete 1, could you tell us briefly what you found in your excavation of the Lazete 2 grave?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Well, at Lazete 2 we recovered 16 bodies. I believe 26 body parts, and even more evidence than Lazete 1; we recovered 872 items of evidence, most of those being shell casings. We did encounter the fact that the grave had been excavated several times before we excavated it. In other words, there was an initial excavation, then there was a robbing event when some bodies were extracted from this grave, and this -- this could be seen again by the presence of body parts and also by the presence of truncated bodies at edges of the robbing areas. But also there had been two excavations within the big grave. I think those -- we call Lazete 2A and Lazete 2B. The entire grave was about 38 metres in length, about four metres in width, and about a metre fifty in depth as well. But it was a very big grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And, as again with Lazete 1, is it correct that the division of responsibility between yourselves and the pathologists in the morgue were such that you just handed over the human remains and didn't participate in the autopsy work?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Yes, we followed the same exact procedure. We exhumed the bodies, put them inside body bags, and then placed them side a refrigerated container, which was later taken to the Visoko, the morgue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I have to further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Elderkin. I have -- Ms. Condon?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, have we received the report from the witness on Lazete 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, no, you haven't. This report -- I could perhaps ask Mr. Peccerelli to explain, but since this report was only prepared very recently, then it's been disclosed to the Defence as part of Mr. Peccerelli's materials but it is not something that we have proposed to admit as an expert's report. So you will have only have, I think, the Lazete 1 report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then to that extent -- how can Mr. Peccerelli be a 92 ter witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I understand the 92 ter application would allow his written evidence on the Lazete 1 report to come in as his 92 ter basis, and then my brief direct examination would be the entire body of evidence presented on Lazete 2, and then any further questions, particularly on that topic, from the Defence would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm happy with that. So as far as Lazete 2 is concerned, this witness gave evidence live, we can take it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: If that's acceptable to Your Honours, that's all that we propose on Lazete 2, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We can live with that, Mr. Elderkin, unless we hear objections from any of the Defence teams. What happened to my -- I've lost everything here. I lost my LiveNote. Yes, Mr. Bourgon. I can still follow on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Of course we were perfectly able to continue the way it is right now, understanding that he has now testified on the Lazete 2 report, live.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Of course, later on when we object to the report, because there will be no need because he testified live, then this will be our -- this is the position we risk taking. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, having said I had finished my examination-in-chief, I wonder whether I might ask to be permitted to have one more question of the witness. It's a very short question, but I'm in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon. Madam Fauveau. Yes, go ahead, Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Many thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Mr. Peccerelli, if I could just ask you, when you mentioned the prior excavation of Lazete 2 by the PHR team, do you recall who it was who led that team?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Bill Haglund.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: That's all, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much. Now, we have on our list that the Nikolic Defence team, the Gvero defence team, and the Borovcanin Defence team do not wish to cross-examine this witness. Can we have a confirmation of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes, from Gvero team.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, for the Nikolic team.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Same for Borovcanin team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, so that's confirmed. Now, that leaves us with the Pandurevic team, the Miletic team, Beara, and Popovic. Who is going to go first? Ms. Condon.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Mr. Peccerelli, you've indicated that your training is as a forensic anthropologist. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: But in your capacity on these particular sites you were operating as an archaeologist?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: I was operating as a deputy senior archaeologist, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Perhaps can you assist me to determine which particular function were you performing on the sites in 2000, were you an anthropologist or were you an archaeologist?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Well, in the United States archaeologist is part of anthropology. It's one of the four subfields, so it depends the way you look at it. I was performing the task of recovering bodies, making sure that we were documenting the entire site, and, although I describe myself as a forensic anthropologist, I have worked on hundreds of recoveries of sites in Guatemala.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. Perhaps specifically insofar as your role or your training as an anthropologist is concerned, that enables to engage in a process of estimating the age of remains, does it not?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: In the proper setting, it does. Within a morgue it would, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And given what your answer has been, that you primarily were there to recover bodies, I take it that you engaged in no process of aging the remains that you found here. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: In the field that would be very difficult so we couldn't do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Well -- and you then subsequently didn't have any role at the morgue in that regard either?
